newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland's DCC sees continued overall growth.
newsitem.headline: Ireland's DCC sees continued overall growth.

text.p: Irish industrial holding group DCC Plc on Monday announced higher annual profits and dividends and said it was confident for the future, with growth expected in all its businesses in the current year.

Pretax profit at DCC, active in the computer, healthcare, food and energy industries, rose 22 percent to 35.3 million Irish pounds ($53.7 million) in the year to March 31, 1997. Turnover was up 17 percent at 627.7 million.

"DCC's consistent record of strong growth continues with these results...Each of DCC's four divisions is budgeting for growth in the current year and the group's financial strength and cash flows will support their continued acquisition and development activity," chief executive and deputy chairman Jim Flavin said in a statement.
The company said it planned to pay a final net dividend of 4.96 Irish pence per share, bringing the total dividend to 8.00 pence, up 16 percent from a year earlier.

DCC said its computer services division, DCC SerCom, raised sales by 22 percent to 202 million Irish pounds while operating profit surged 36 percent to just over 10 million, helped by a satisfactory performance at its manufacturing services business Printech Group.

DCC Foods saw profit rise 17 percent to nine million pounds on a 22 percent increase in sales to 221 million, with the trend towards eating out, healthy eating and snacking helping business, DCC said.
Earnings at DCC Healthcare surged 70 percent to 5.13 million pounds, helped by the first full-year contribution from DMA, the Welsh manufacturer of mobility and rehabilitation products.

But profits at DCC Energy dipped 10 percent to 7.3 million pounds because of pressure on margins after a steep rise in product costs. Turnover rose 17 percent to 118 million pounds. ($ = 0.657 Irish Pounds)
